beats.title: Free African Society Founded
beats.description: Black Philadelphians led by Richard Allen and Absalom Jones formed a mutual aid group, an early organisation for Black self-help and dignity.

beats.title: Walker's Appeal Is Published
beats.description: A Boston clothier printed a fiery pamphlet urging Black Americans to resist oppression and demand the rights promised to all.

beats.title: Crandall's School for Black Girls
beats.description: A Connecticut teacher admitted Black girls to her academy, provoking a boycott and laws aimed at shutting the school down.

beats.title: Fourteenth Amendment Ratified
beats.description: A constitutional amendment promised citizenship and equal protection of the laws to everyone born in the country, including freed Black Americans.

beats.title: Fifteenth Amendment Ratified
beats.description: A new amendment barred the denial of the vote on grounds of race, giving Black men the franchise on paper.

beats.title: First Federal Civil Rights Act
beats.description: Congress outlawed racial discrimination in inns, theatres and public transport, a law later struck down and long unenforced.

beats.title: Wells Publishes Southern Horrors
beats.description: A Memphis journalist used careful reporting to expose the myths used to excuse mob violence and launched a campaign against it.

beats.title: Gandhi Is Thrown Off a Train
beats.description: A young lawyer holding a first-class ticket was ejected at a South African station for his skin colour, sparking his resistance to discrimination.
beats.why_in: start of Gandhi's fight against racial discrimination

beats.title: Plessy v. Ferguson Ruling
beats.description: The Supreme Court ruled that separate facilities for Black and white citizens were constitutional, if supposedly equal.
beats.why_in: landmark segregation case that civil rights fought
beats.note: Included as an example beat; it is the ruling the movement fought.

beats.title: Du Bois's Souls of Black Folk
beats.description: A scholar's collection of essays on the colour line challenged accommodation and demanded full civil rights for Black Americans.

beats.title: NAACP Is Founded
beats.description: A biracial group of activists met in New York to form an association to fight racial injustice and secure equal rights.
beats.why_in: founding of leading civil rights body

beats.title: Native National Congress Founded
beats.description: Black leaders gathered in Bloemfontein to form the organisation that would become the ANC and lead the struggle against white minority rule.

beats.title: Garvey Founds the UNIA
beats.description: Marcus Garvey launched a Jamaican organisation promoting Black pride, self-reliance and unity across the African diaspora.

beats.title: First Pan-African Congress in Paris
beats.description: Black leaders from Africa, the Caribbean and America met alongside the post-war peace talks to press for racial equality and colonial reform.

beats.title: Pullman Porters Form Their Union
beats.description: A.Philip Randolph organised Black sleeping-car workers into a union, a base that later powered national civil rights protests.

beats.title: Negro History Week Begins
beats.description: Historian Carter Woodson launched a week celebrating Black achievement, the seed of what became a month of national commemoration.

beats.title: Bethune Founds the National Council
beats.description: Educator Mary McLeod Bethune united Black women's groups into a national council to lobby for equality and a voice in government.

beats.title: Marian Anderson at Lincoln Memorial
beats.description: After a patriotic society refused her its hall, the contralto performed on the steps of a national monument before a vast crowd.

beats.title: Roosevelt Bans War Industry Bias
beats.description: Facing a threatened mass march on the capital, the president ordered an end to racial discrimination in war industries.
beats.why_in: executive order won by civil rights pressure

beats.title: Truman Desegregates the Military
beats.description: An executive order declared equal treatment for all service members regardless of race, ending formal segregation in the military.

beats.title: Brown v. Board of Education
beats.description: The Supreme Court unanimously ruled that separate public schools for Black and white children were inherently unequal.
beats.note: Court ruling, but the signature civil rights victory; included as an example beat.

beats.title: Montgomery Bus Boycott Begins
beats.description: After Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat, Black residents stopped riding the city's buses for over a year.

beats.title: March on Washington
beats.description: A quarter of a million people rallied at the Lincoln Memorial for jobs and freedom, where Martin Luther King Jr. spoke of his dream.

beats.title: Civil Rights Act Signed
beats.description: A sweeping law outlawed segregation in public places and discrimination in employment on grounds of race, colour, religion, sex or origin.

beats.title: Selma to Montgomery Marches
beats.description: Marchers beaten on a bridge at Selma drew national outrage and helped push through a law protecting Black voting rights.

beats.title: Soweto Uprising
beats.description: Black schoolchildren marched against being taught in Afrikaans, and police gunfire turned the protest into a nationwide revolt.

beats.title: MLK Day Signed Into Law
beats.description: The president signed a bill creating a national holiday honouring the slain civil rights leader, after a long campaign for it.
beats.why_in: national recognition of civil rights leader

beats.title: Tutu Wins the Nobel Peace Prize
beats.description: The Anglican archbishop was honoured for his peaceful opposition to apartheid, bringing the cause fresh world attention.

beats.title: Nelson Mandela Is Freed
beats.description: After more than 27 years behind bars, the anti-apartheid leader walked out of prison to cheering crowds.

beats.title: Mandela Wins First Multiracial Vote
beats.description: Millions of Black South Africans voted for the first time, and the contest brought Nelson Mandela to the presidency.

beats.title: South Africa Signs New Constitution
beats.description: The president signed a founding charter guaranteeing equality and banning discrimination, replacing the legacy of racial rule.

beats.title: UN Anti-Racism Conference, Durban
beats.description: Delegates gathered in a South African city for a world conference on racism, xenophobia and related intolerance.

beats.title: Barack Obama Elected President
beats.description: American voters chose the first Black president, a milestone many saw as the fruit of the long struggle for equality.

beats.title: Black Lives Matter Is Born
beats.description: A social media hashtag, created after a controversial acquittal, grew into a global movement against racism and police violence.

beats.title: Ferguson Protests
beats.description: The fatal police shooting of a Black teenager in a Missouri suburb set off days of unrest and a national debate on policing and race.

beats.title: George Floyd Protests Go Global
beats.description: The killing of a Black man by a police officer in Minneapolis triggered huge demonstrations for racial justice in many countries.
